lacuna.current_status: Read 2026-09-15. (1) NCCL at decode message sizes: NCCL auto-selects algorithm by topology and message size - Ring/Tree plus NVLS (2.17+) and CollNetDirect/CollnetChain (2.14+), where "NVLS and NVLSTree enable NVLink SHARP offload" (NCCL user guide env docs) - and protocol LL/LL128/Simple; the historical thresholds (NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD, NCCL_TREE_THRESHOLD, removed in 2.5) encoded the rule that LL protocols serve small latency-bound messages and trees beat rings at small sizes. "Demystifying NCCL: An In-depth Analysis of GPU Communication" (arXiv:2507.04786, submitted 2025-07-07, NCCL 2.19.1 on GH200) states: "LL/LL128 are chosen for small messages to reduce latency, while Simple is used for larger messages", LL/LL128 "perform best for small messages (less than 64 KiB)", LL reaches only 25-50% of peak bandwidth, and quantifies per-hop protocol latency as Simple ~6 us, LL ~1 us, LL128 ~2 us. (2) Newest measured datapoint for one-shot vs NCCL: Shen et al., 'Every us Matters: Achieving Near Speed-of-Light Latency in GPU Collectives' (arXiv:2607.16100, 2026-07-17): on 4x GB200, "reduces average latency for small messages from 11.0 us for NCCL ring to 2.37 us"; the measured 2-GPU speed-of-light allreduce there is L_SoL = 2 x L2_RTT (0.306 us) + remote_store (0.792 us) = 1.404 us, with their one-shot kernel ~7% over SoL at 2 GPUs; a ~5 us small-message AR on 4 GPUs spends ~40% of latency in two barrier calls, each >1 us. (3) Serving-stack alternatives: vLLM's custom_all_reduce (vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py, read at main 2026-09-15; vLLM docs v0.11.0 describe it as derived from TensorRT-LLM's implementation) - supported world sizes {2,4,6,8}(16 via MNNVL only), allreduce cap 8 MiB further clamped by per-arch/per-world-size caps, dtypes fp16/fp32/bf16, input size must satisfy inp_size % 16 == 0, requires a full-mesh P2P topology ("not supported on more than two PCIe-only GPUs"), and is CUDA-graph-safe: a capture() context "records all the buffer addresses used in the CUDA graph" via register_graph_buffers; the module notes the eager-path staging memcpy "should be small (<=1% of overall latency)" and that "for 4 or more non NVLink-capable GPUs, custom allreduce provides little performance improvement over NCCL". vLLM issue #8457 (2024 [uncertain: exact month]) records that TensorRT-LLM-style per-load acquire fences cost "about 6us latency" in this kernel class - fence semantics are first-order at single-digit-us sizes. TensorRT-LLM v0.19.0 release notes (~Mar 2025 [uncertain: month]): "Added one-shot version for UserBuffer AllReduce-Normalization on FP16/BF16" (one-shot AR fused with residual+RMSNorm) and a heuristic routing custom-AR vs NCCL by message size; NVIDIA's '3x Faster AllReduce with NVSwitch and TensorRT-LLM MultiShot' blog (2025) covers the NVSwitch-multicast side, inapplicable here. llama.cpp: docs/multi-gpu.md (read 2026-09-15) - the new '-sm tensor' mode "uses [NCCL] automatically for cross-GPU reductions" when built with -DGGML_CUDA_NCCL=ON (default on), the older row-split path is deprecated as "comparatively poor performance", and CUDA P2P is opt-in "usually restricted to workstation/datacenter GPUs" - org prior art sinter (CONSOLIDATION.md T9) is exactly such a llama.cpp megakernel that tied the DRAM floor on this silicon. PyTorch async-TP (torchtitan announcement, discuss.pytorch.org, Oct 2024): micro-pipelined all-gather/reduce-scatter overlapped into GEMMs via symmetric memory - explicitly "optimized for large matmul problems". (4) CUDA-graph interaction: NCCL ops capturable since 2.9 (requires CUDA >= 11.3, per the NCCL CUDA-graphs user guide); capture must be uniform across ranks; mixing captured and non-captured NCCL work can deadlock (NCCL_GRAPH_MIXING_SUPPORT); user-buffer registration (ncclCommRegister / NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER, since 2.11) is a performance feature "when ... the CollNet algorithm is used" - i.e., irrelevant on this pair. vLLM's custom AR needs no such registration machinery: buffers are registered at graph capture by register_graph_buffers. (5) Measured on this silicon: host plan/0004 protocol measured 43.7 GB/s on the NVLink path; Quadro RTX 6000 datasheet: NVLink "Connects 2 Quadro RTX 6000 GPUs", 100 GB/s bidirectional (2 links x 25 GB/s per direction); Puget Systems (2018-10-16) on 2x RTX 2080 NVLink: p2pBandwidthLatencyTest 24.23 GB/s unidirectional / 48.37 GB/s bidirectional and GPU-GPU latency 0.92 us vs 11-20 us over PCIe.
lacuna.applicability: Everything NVSwitch-class is arch-blocked on the TU102 pair and must not be planned for: NVLS/NVLSTree and CollNet need NVLink SHARP/NVSwitch (Hopper/NVSwitch systems), NCCL 2.27's symmetric-memory windowed kernels and vLLM's MNNVL/symmetric-memory one-shot paths need Blackwell-class or Hopper multicast (vLLM source: "MNNVL is available only on Blackwell-class GPUs"). On this pair NCCL runs plain Ring (at 2 ranks a single P2P exchange) over LL/LL128 - functional, and not worth tuning: at 20-41 KB the call is latency, not bandwidth, and the NCCL docs warn that forced NCCL_PROTO/NCCL_ALGO overrides (and "enabling LL128 on platforms that don't support it") cause corruption or hangs and "should not be kept in production". What does transfer and is the actionable core: the P2P ld/st + flag one-shot custom AR (vLLM/TRT-LLM lineage) is sm_70-class portable - no multicast, no CollNet, works over the 2-link Turing bridge at fp16, and the host payloads pass vLLM's size gate (batch 4 x 2560 x fp16 = 20,480 B; batch 8 = 40,960 B; both divisible by 16). The engine already carries this code (vLLM V1 lineage); whether the fork's TP2 path actually dispatches it (vs NCCL fallback) is a one-probe question. Overlap strategies (async-TP, microbatch overlap) have no headroom here: at batch 4 the GEMMs are byte-regime with zero idle compute to hide communication under, and the AR's wire time is 0.47 us - the only overlap-adjacent win is launch-count fusion (AR+residual+RMSNorm in one kernel, TRT-LLM v0.19.0 style, portable to sm_75). The relevant cost model for the floor: the record's floor-anchored target already reserves "minus TP2 allreduce overhead"; this item prices that clause.

design.mechanism: MEASURE, THEN PRICE, THEN (ONLY IF NEEDED) SWAP OR FUSE. Step 1 - confirm dispatch: one gate-1 probe reads whether the engine's TP2 path uses the custom AR or NCCL (vLLM logs the custom-AR disabled_reason; VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK exists because driver P2P reports can lie; NCCL_DEBUG=INFO if NCCL is active). Expectation: custom AR active on a P2P-capable world_size=2 pair. Step 2 - price the step share from the plan/0010 #step-profile ledger: 64 AR nodes/step at batch 4 (2 per layer x 32 layers [uncertain: confirm 1 vs 2 ARs in the 24 GDN layers - the source read shows the dense-path out_proj AR via reduce_results; the in-projection split may add a second site]). Payload per call: 4 x 2560 x 2 B = 20,480 B (batch 8: 40,960 B). Wire time: 20,480 / 43.7 GB/s (host-measured, plan/0004) = 0.47 us - irrelevant; per-call latency dominates. Expected per-call on this pair: one-shot custom AR ~3-7 us [uncertain: extrapolated, not measured here - anchors: 2-GPU SoL 1.404 us and measured 2.37 us one-shot on GB200 (arXiv:2607.16100, 2026-07-17); ~0.92 us P2P latency on Turing NVLink (Puget 2018); ~6 us fence cost named in vLLM #8457]. Expected step share: 64 x 3-7 us = 0.19-0.45 ms/step = 0.8-2.5% of an 18.0-24.3 ms step (0.19/24.27 = 0.78%; 0.45/18.02 = 2.50%). If NCCL were dispatching instead: 10-25 us/call (LL-protocol small-message class; NCCL ring small-message 11.0 us even on GB200) = 0.64-1.60 ms/step = 2.6-8.8%. Floor integration: the one-shot case adds 0.19-0.45 ms to the 17.83 ms byte floor (17.70 weights + 0.12 KV + 0.01 activations), giving T_floor ~ 18.0-18.3 ms. Step 3 - remediate only on ledger evidence: if the engine is on NCCL or the ledger shows >1 ms AR, adopt the vLLM custom one-shot AR (upstream in the engine's own lineage, graph-capturable via register_graph_buffers, P2P over the bridge, fp16) - configuration, not kernel work; re-verify the p2p check stays ON (IOMMU/BIOS can silently kill bridge P2P - the llama.cpp doc caveat). Step 4 - the further lever is fusion, not protocol: a TRT-LLM v0.19.0-style one-shot AR+residual+RMSNorm kernel folds the two post-GEMM ops plus the collective into one launch at 64 sites, cutting ~64-128 graph nodes/step (~0.1-0.3 ms at 1-2 us/node [uncertain]) and one global sync per site; portable to sm_75 (P2P one-shot + warp reductions + norm math in-kernel). It stacks with the step-structure/megakernel surgeries itemized elsewhere in this corpus; it does not stand alone. Step 5 - record the fitted a+b*s AR latency constants into the calx-mill TU102 adapter (the step-roofline-method item's collective model), measured here, closing the 'minus TP2 allreduce overhead' clause of the floor rule with a number instead of a reservation.
design.failure_modes: (1) Fence semantics: weakening per-load acquire/release for latency (the vLLM #8457 direction) trades directly against memory-ordering correctness under graph replay - one misordered flag read corrupts silently at replay time; the exact-execution oracle must cover the AR path (gate-0 precedent: the banked 6e-5 rel tolerance class). (2) Graph capture: allocations during capture break replay - vLLM's register_graph_buffers exists for this; NCCL under graphs with multiple GPUs per process can deadlock (NCCL CUDA-graphs guide recommends one GPU per process) - the host already runs one GPU per rank; NCCL's capture must be uniform across ranks, so a conditional AR on one rank only is a hang. (3) Silent dispatch fallback: vLLM's custom AR refuses odd shapes (inp_size % 16 gate) and non-full-mesh P2P, falling back to NCCL without fanfare - verify per shape (batch 4-8 both pass) rather than assuming; VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK hides real bridge failures. (4) Reduction-order drift: a fused AR(+norm) kernel changes fp16 accumulation order vs the incumbent path - gate-0 oracle with the banked tie-break discipline before any A/B (the plan/0009 fp16 tie-break class). (5) Protocol overrides: forcing NCCL_PROTO/NCCL_ALGO per a blog table risks LL128 corruption on unsupported platforms and violates the NCCL docs' production warning - leave selection automatic. (6) Measured-not-spec'd: 43.7 GB/s host-measured vs 50 GB/s datasheet per-direction share vs 24 GB/s on consumer 2080s (Puget 2018, possibly test-limited) - three different numbers for 'NVLink bandwidth'; only the host-measured one enters the model, re-measured per driver. (7) Engine-context inflation: the banked inversion precedent (a sub-ms kernel costing ~3.6 ms/step in-engine, MEMORY.md 2026-09-13) means the AR's ledger-measured share, not this item's estimate, is the deciding number - hence measure-first.
design.effort_estimate: Measurement-first: one gate-1 session (ledger read of the 64 AR nodes + dispatch check) - hours, CPU/GPU-light. The custom-AR swap (only on fallback evidence) is configuration - under a day including a committed-row re-check. The fused AR+residual+RMSNorm one-shot kernel is the only kernel-lane item: ~2-4 days (kernel + oracle + graph-capture integration) and is worth it only stacked with the step-structure surgeries.
design.priority_signal: Below the sensitivity floor as estimated: 0.19-0.45 ms/step (custom one-shot active) is sub-multi-ms and will not move committed rows; even the NCCL-fallback bound (0.64-1.60 ms) is borderline. Against the ~4.3 ms residual it is at most a quarter of the gap, and the engine bisect (2026-09-10) already exonerated NCCL as the variance owner. It becomes load-bearing only on ledger contradiction: if the #step-profile ledger prices the AR above ~1 ms (fallback, or the engine-interaction inflation precedent), the swap is then the cheapest multi-tenth-ms recovery available. Verdict: spend the one ledger read now (it is already a named output column of #step-profile: 'allreduce time per step'); spend kernel-lane days only on fusion, and only stacked.

sources: Siyuan Shen, Tiancheng Chen, Torsten Hoefler, Anton Korzh, John Bachan, et al. (NVIDIA/ETH) - 'Every us Matters: Achieving Near Speed-of-Light Latency in GPU Collectives', arXiv:2607.16100 (2026-07-17): NCCL ring small-message 11.0 us vs 2.37 us one-shot on 4x GB200; 2-GPU SoL allreduce 1.404 us (2 x 0.306 L2_RTT + 0.792 remote_store); barriers >1 us each, ~40% of a 5 us AR. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16100

'Demystifying NCCL: An In-depth Analysis of GPU Communication', arXiv:2507.04786 (2025-07-07, NCCL 2.19.1, GH200 testbed): LL/LL128 for messages < 64 KiB, Simple for large; per-hop latency Simple ~6 us, LL ~1 us, LL128 ~2 us; LL at 25-50% of peak bandwidth; Ring for large, Tree better small. https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04786

NVIDIA NCCL user guide (read 2026-09-15): env docs - NCCL_ALGO (Ring, Tree, CollnetChain/Direct 2.14+, NVLS 2.17+, 'NVLS and NVLSTree enable NVLink SHARP offload'), NCCL_PROTO (LL/LL128/Simple; 'enabling LL128 on platforms that don't support it can lead to data corruption'; overrides discouraged in production); CUDA-graphs page - 'Starting with NCCL 2.9, NCCL operations can be captured by CUDA Graphs' (CUDA >= 11.3), uniform-capture and deadlock caveats, NCCL_GRAPH_REGISTER (2.11+) a CollNet-only registration gain. https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/env.html and .../usage/cudagraph.html

vLLM custom_all_reduce source (vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py, main, read 2026-09-15) and module docs (v0.11.0): world sizes {2,4,6,8}, 8 MiB cap + per-arch caps, fp16/fp32/bf16, inp_size % 16 == 0, full-mesh P2P required, graph capture via capture()/register_graph_buffers; derived from TensorRT-LLM's custom AR. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py ; https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.11.0/api/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.html

vLLM issue #8457 'Add weaker memory fence for custom allreduce' (2024 [uncertain: month]): TensorRT-LLM-style acquire/release per-load fences cost 'about 6us latency' in one-shot-class AR kernels. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/8457

TensorRT-LLM v0.19.0 release notes (~Mar 2025 [uncertain: month]): 'Added one-shot version for UserBuffer AllReduce-Normalization on FP16/BF16'; custom-AR heuristic routing to NCCL by message size. https://nvidia.github.io/TensorRT-LLM/0.19.0/release-notes.html

NVIDIA Developer Blog - '3x Faster AllReduce with NVSwitch and TensorRT-LLM MultiShot' (2025): NVSwitch-multicast AR, the NVSwitch-class line inapplicable to a 2-GPU NVLink-bridge pair. https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/3x-faster-allreduce-with-nvswitch-and-tensorrt-llm-multishot/

NVIDIA Developer Blog - 'Enabling Fast Inference and Resilient Training with NCCL 2.27' (2025): symmetric-memory kernels, 'up to 9x reduction in latency for small message sizes' - NVSwitch-class feature, arch-blocked on sm_75 bridge pairs. https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/enabling-fast-inference-and-resilient-training-with-nccl-2-27/

llama.cpp docs/multi-gpu.md (read 2026-09-15): '-sm tensor' mode uses NCCL automatically for cross-GPU reductions (GGML_CUDA_NCCL=ON default); row-split deprecated; GGML_CUDA_P2P 'usually restricted to workstation/datacenter GPUs'. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/multi-gpu.md

PyTorch Forum (torchtitan) - 'Introducing Async Tensor Parallelism in PyTorch' (Oct 2024): micro-pipelined AG/RS overlap via symmetric memory, 'optimized for large matmul problems' - no headroom at M=4 decode. https://discuss.pytorch.org/t/distributed-w-torchtitan-introducing-async-tensor-parallelism-in-pytorch/209487

Puget Systems - 'NVLink on RTX 2080 TensorFlow and Peer-to-Peer Performance with Linux' (2018-10-16): 2x RTX 2080 NVLink p2pBandwidthLatencyTest - 24.23 GB/s unidirectional, 48.37 GB/s bidirectional, GPU-GPU latency 0.92 us vs 11-20 us PCIe. https://www.pugetsystems.com/labs/hpc/nvlink-on-rtx-2080-tensorflow-and-peer-to-peer-performance-with-linux-1262/
